title: Custom Logger does not log C# exceptions when running from Godot editor
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7628) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700K CPU @ 4.00GHz (8 threads) - 15.95 GiB memory

### Issue description

When using the [Logger](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_logger.html) class to register a custom logger, exceptions emitted by C# code do not get logged by the custom logger when the game is being run from the Godot editor.

This does work when running the game using the launcher directly and clicking run on the project and when exporting the project to an executable.

### Steps to reproduce

### Steps
1. Register custom logger
2. Trigger exceptions from C# code while running app from Godot editor
3. Observe the exceptions are not logged.
4. Trigger exceptions from C# code while running app from Godot launcher
5. Observe the exceptions are logged

### MRP overview
Minimal reproduction uses a logger which triggers an alert for any message. There are two scripts attached to nodes, one C# which throws an exception on the first frame, and one in GDScript which throws an exception on the first frame. When running this in the editor we only see one exception (from GDScript). When running from the godot project selection page, we see two exceptions (from GDScript and C#).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[loggerissue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24808223/loggerissue.zip)
